meanings: verb: to follow; to chase
verb: to try to achieve (a dream or goal)
examples: The baby elephant ran, but the pack of lions pursued it.
Man pursued the dream of flight for hundreds of years before the modern airplane was invented.

meanings: verb: to be aware of; to sense or feel
examples: If hunters are skilled, the animals will not perceive their presence.

meanings: noun: a rule or idea that makes the base for a system (often moral)
examples: The principles at the heart of the new religion are the same as many central beliefs of Christianity.

meanings: verb: to create; to produce (especially energy)
examples: Movement generates heat.

meanings: noun: the appearance of objects from a particular direction
noun: a point of view; an opinion
examples: Young children's drawings do not have clearly defined perspective; you may see three walls of an outside of a building, for example.
Many Hollywood movies, when watched from a woman's perspective, have clearly sexist characters.

meanings: verb: to be made of
examples: The U.S. consists of fifty states.

meanings: adjective: immediately after
examples: Both the winter and the subsequent spring were surprisingly dry, with neither snow nor rain.

meanings: verb: to make easier
examples: Classical music, unlike many types of music, will generally facilitate learning and improve memory.

meanings: noun: a structure for a building, system, or idea
examples: Ellen's business plan may have failed, but it formed the framework for her next, successful plan.

meanings: verb: to make people follow (a rule or law)
examples: Although smoking is not allowed on school campus, the ban isn't enforced, and many students smoke freely.

meanings: noun: a fact that influences or changes a result
examples: Two of the largest factors affecting children's healthy growth are food and relationships with parents.

meanings: verb: to come out of
examples: After a winter spent sleeping, the bear emerges from its cave.

meanings: adjective: from a reasonable or correct basis
examples: Many people have said the artist Jackson Pollack's work didn't require much skill, and that idea is somewhat valid.

meanings: adjective: central; of fundamental importance
noun: the center of something
examples: Although we have made improvements in brain science, many of the core problems remain.
The earth's core is made of liquid rock.

meanings: verb: to watch the quality or progress of something over time
noun: something or somebody which monitors
examples: We have been carefully monitoring the amount of salt in our oceans for the last 50 years.
Heart rate monitors can be used for both medicine and exercise.

meanings: verb: (usually "be derived from") to come from; originate from
examples: Many European languages are derived at least partly from Latin.

meanings: verb: to keep; to continue to have or contain
examples: Originally from France, Jean retains a hint of her French accent even today.

meanings: verb: to agree to give (something that was asked for)
verb: to admit; to say something is true
examples: The government has recently granted us access to information that was secret before.
I disagree that snakes make good pets, but I'll grant that they're easy to take care of.

meanings: adjective: forming the basis for something
examples: There is no single way to put an end to drug addiction since there are many underlying causes.

meanings: verb: to not include; to keep out of a list or group
examples: I eat almost anything, excluding spicy foods. I hate hot peppers.

meanings: noun: the size or amount of something compared to the whole or other parts
examples: Cartoons of people often have exaggerated proportions, such as very large eyes or hands.

meanings: noun: a large plan
noun: the system by which something is arranged
examples: Microsoft's marketing scheme for their new tablet computer was less than successful.
The modern scheme for naming different types of plants and animals started around 1800.

meanings: verb: to do or perform (something very negative, like a crime)
verb: to promise; to make a final and unchangeable decision
verb: (usually "be committed to") to give all of your energy to something
examples: Michiko committed too many grammar errors in her essay, and that hurt her score.
Before you commit to a university, be sure to spend some time on campus.
I'm completely committed to our baseball team's success; I'd do anything to win.

meanings: verb: to be the pieces that make a whole
examples: Fifty states constitute the U.S.A.

meanings: verb: to come to a conclusion through logic and evidence; to figure out
examples: By analyzing the bones, we can deduce when the animal lived and, maybe, how it died.

meanings: adjective: having many different types
examples: The student population is incredibly diverse at South State University, with students from 30 different countries.

meanings: verb: to start (a rule or system)
noun: a group or organization that studies or works for something specific
examples: In January, we will institute a plan to make car accidents less frequent.
The National Cancer Institute was created to learn more about, and hopefully cure, the many types of cancer.

meanings: noun: a period of time in a longer process of change
examples: There are at least three different phases in a frog's development from egg to adult.

meanings: noun: a goal
adjective: based in fact; not an opinion; not from personal beliefs or ideas
examples: The objective of the TOEFL is to measure your total English ability.
We can objectively measure how spicy a pepper is, but how we feel about that spiciness is not objective.

meanings: verb: to give a good reason for an action or situation (especially one that seems bad)
examples: Although Milos explained for a long time, he could not justify borrowing his brother's car without asking.

meanings: noun: a range of subjects or studies; a field; a discipline
examples: Researchers working in many different areas, from psychology to physics, will be able to use the new type of plastic.

meanings: noun: the health and happiness of a person or group
examples: A perfect government would care more about the welfare of its people than anything else.

meanings: noun: an effect that changes a situation
verb: to affect strongly
noun: the force of being hit hard
examples: The end of the war had a large impact on economic growth.
My father's advice hugely impacted my university decision.
The impact of a car crash can send a driver who doesn't wear a seat belt through the window.

meanings: noun: the amount or volume something can hold
noun: ability (especially mental)
examples: The hotel is full to maximum capacity; there are no empty rooms.
Few birds have the capacity to recognize themselves when looking in a mirror; most act as though there is a second bird behind the glass.

meanings: adjective: outside (especially of a body or system)
examples: Uncontrollable, external events can cause even a very careful company to fail.

meanings: noun: a thing that exists or acts as one
examples: The male angler fish will attach permanently to the female, and in time, the two fish will become a single entity.

meanings: verb: to correct a problem with another positive thing
examples: The pay at Ian's new job was low, but the freedom his boss gave him compensated for that.

meanings: verb: to become a part of
examples: It is difficult to smoothly integrate a small, foreign culture into the main culture of a country.

meanings: adjective: separate; not the same thing and with no parts in common
examples: Your left arm and right arm are controlled by two discrete areas of the brain.

meanings: adjective: clearly seen or understood
adjective: seeming (but not definitely true)
examples: After only a few months, it was apparent that the French would not win the war.
The shark's apparent sleepiness is actually because of how cold the water is.

meanings: noun: a rule made by an organization, government, or company
examples: School policy does not allow alcohol on campus.

meanings: verb: to make not true or not effective
examples: Studying late into the night might help you learn more, but sleeping less negates the positive effects.

meanings: verb: to look for; to search
examples: Across many different cultures' stories, heroes seek more than just gold or fame.

meanings: verb: to limit the activity of; to restrict
examples: Popular belief says that a pet fish's size is constrained by the size of the tank it's in, but this is actually false.

meanings: noun: the measures by which something is judged or decided
examples: A good TOEFL essay meets a few criteria, including good structure, clear ideas, and natural vocabulary.

meanings: verb: to work or communicate with the different people, groups, or pieces involved in a large project
examples: A chef at a big restaurant will spend his time coordinating all of the menus and other workers, not cooking.

meanings: verb: (usually "to be oriented") to move into a position in line with some specific point
verb: (usually "to orient yourself") to explore and become comfortable with
examples: The statues appear to be oriented toward the sunrise.
It took a few weeks to orient myself in the new job, but I feel comfortable now.

meanings: noun: a part of a whole
examples: Many electronics are made of thousands of smaller components and wires.

meanings: noun: a feature, a characteristic, a particular part of something
examples: The three most important aspects to think about when learning a language are grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation.

meanings: verb: to change; to adjust
examples: Magazines heavily alter the photos they publish of celebrities.
